opportunity: A printf/scanf call states the types of its variadic arguments in its format string, but reading it cost a second decompile of every caller: Ghidra's FormatStringAnalyzer is DecompilerDependent, so the format pointer is only visible as an input varnode of a lifted CALL. decompile-all measured +77.5% (cronie crontab), +55.1% (gnutls psktool), +43.7% (gzip), which held the option to a per-run opt-in and out of the aggressive preset, even though the recovery was real (decbench C type_match perfects 80 -> 88 of 1,133). The constant is in the image, and so is the call site.

round6.root_cause: Not a formatstring bug but its interaction with P4 trial scoring (upstream onlyOpUse/checkCallDoubleUse): x3 = len (subs w3,w2,#192) also reaches the error-path fprintf through mov w2,w3. An OPEN fprintf excuses the use while its own trial is unscored; a CLOSED one never does, so x3 is vetoed at both parse_rtattr sites. Trace (temporary eprintln in only_op_use): under off the fprintf at 0x42ff7c was still unscored; main already drops parse_rtattr's len at 13/60 ip sites, and at the 9 traced the veto is the same mov w2,w3; bl fprintf 'BUG: wrong nlmsg len'. static: 15/60.
